correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening on the Perote–Villa Aldama side
correspondence.finding: The Perote relief original depicts the Puerco feeder descending north from the Cofre de Perote slope and a separate western drainage pattern toward the Perote plain. The selected opening and its northwestward excursion lie west of the depicted Puerco route, across the intervening slope/plain setting. Neither this municipal map nor the state original depicts a stream connecting that chosen excursion through to the northbound feeder. This is more than an unresolved precise source point or minor bend. The later return toward the Las Vigas de Ramírez approach is visible, but the initial through-link remains unestablished. No claim is made that a real local connection cannot exist.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Vigas de Ramírez to Piedra Parada and the northbound valley
correspondence.finding: After the opening excursion, the selection follows the depicted northeast-running feeder through the Las Vigas de Ramírez setting toward Piedra Parada. The source shows its joining approach from the southwest, the separate eastern Tatatila approach, and the turn north into the Bobos valley. These joins and the intervening selected parts correspond at ordinary cartographic scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Named Bobos valley through Zapotitlán, Santiago and the Tlapacoyan approach
correspondence.finding: The selected northward valley follows the blue river directly labeled Río Bobos east of Altotonga and through the Zapotitlán and Santiago setting. Its bends toward the Tlapacoyan approach remain on the connected river. The western Jalacingo/Altotonga drainage and other joining approaches are geographically distinct; their upstream courses are not selected tributary fragments.

correspondence.component_scope: Atenco bend, Martínez de la Torre and the northeast plain approach
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the broad eastward bend by Atenco and repeats Río Bobos directly on the selected course into the Martínez de la Torre–Independencia setting. The selected continuation turns northeast across the plain. Separate northern and southern joining channels are visible; the continuous selected river is distinguished from the more northerly Río El Potrero corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Felipe Carrillo Puerto to El Pital and San Rafael
correspondence.finding: The northeast and eastward selected bends follow the connected river through the Felipe Carrillo Puerto setting to El Pital and the southern approach to San Rafael. All intervening selected parts have a mapped river correspondence. No selected lake, reservoir, canal-transfer or other through-water connector is depicted interrupting this corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: San Rafael bends, Bobos (Nautla) estuary and actual Gulf terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The state map and Nautla relief map depict the selected San Rafael bends continuing into the estuarine waterbody explicitly labeled Bobos (Nautla), with an opening to the Gulf of Mexico. The separate Misantla river lies southeast of this corridor. The final rendered extension reaches the Gulf beside the mapped estuary; it is treated as a generalized coastal extension, without moving its endpoint to the mapped mouth or asserting that its straight last segment traces the exact estuarine channel, bank or shoreline crossing. The ordinary receiving-water and lower-river correspondence is supported.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and initial westward hook
correspondence.finding: The actual southern opening and the complete short northward, westward and reversing sequence lie in mapped Inland Ice south of Warming Land. The original distinguishes this broad ice terrain from the colored exposed-rock tract farther north. The blue ice contours and dashed sub-ice information are not mapped river channels and do not name this selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward passage from Inland Ice into southern Warming Land
correspondence.finding: The long northward part and its westward step continue through the mapped ice terrain to the indented southern exposed-rock margin of Warming Land. The original covers the entire ice-to-land transition and each stored join. The selected passage is geographically accounted for, without inferring a surveyed surface or subglacial stream through the transition.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northward to northeastward exposed-land sequence
correspondence.finding: All thirteen selected parts occupy the southern and middle exposed-rock tract of Warming Land, east of its larger enclosed local-ice area. Original cartography continuously exposes the intervening land, geological boundaries and neighboring ice patches. Those geological lines and nearby pale patches are not evidence for a named natural river or an established lake-throughflow.

correspondence.component_scope: Long northern passage among local ice and rock margins
correspondence.finding: The selected long northward continuation passes through the eastern Warming Land rock and local-ice-margin tract, including the small enclosed ice-area setting before the final westward bend. The complete passage is visible on the original, with nearby blue ice contours and colored land boundaries distinguishable. Its terrain correspondence does not establish river continuity across those land-and-ice surfaces.

correspondence.component_scope: Final westward bend and actual northern ending
correspondence.finding: The final westward series and short northward ending lie in the northern Warming Land exposed-rock setting, west of Sherard Osborn Fjord and north of the local-ice cluster. The original covers the actual supplied ending. At this generalized source scale the ending is in the mapped land tract; it is not independently established as a fjord shoreline or ordinary river mouth. The model sea classification is therefore not promoted to a hydrological claim, and exact modern bank or ice-front positions are not needed for this terrain correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: chosen-eastern-opening
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and initial feeder lie east of the successfully read Spence Bay sheet. No permitted inspected original establishes its initial waterbody/channel setting or first joins. The selected geometry supplies orientation only, and nearby lake labels are not evidence of this missing opening.
correspondence.role: Chosen eastern opening and first northwestern feeder turns

correspondence.component_scope: eastern-bend-and-lake-approach
correspondence.finding: The early western/southwestern turns and the approach to the eastern Spence Bay sheet boundary remain outside the inspected cartography, apart from the continuation at the boundary. The short visible continuation into the western lake does not establish the omitted upstream joins. The first portion of part 6 belongs to this unresolved approach; its mapped western continuation is recorded separately.
correspondence.role: Eastern northward bend, southwestern return and approach to the sheet boundary

correspondence.component_scope: lady-melville-lake-passage
correspondence.finding: At the eastern sheet edge, short blue channels and small connected waters lead into the lake explicitly labelled Lady Melville Lake. The selected western continuation crosses that lake and turns toward its western arm. The lake body and the selected within-sheet corridor are visible together. Straight modeled portions are treated as generalized lake passages rather than exact shoreline crossings; this completes the mapped portion only, without asserting the missing eastern feeder.
correspondence.role: Mapped eastern lake entry, Lady Melville Lake passage and western-arm approach

correspondence.component_scope: lady-melville-to-netsilik-transfer
correspondence.finding: The original depicts a narrow connection from the western Lady Melville Lake arm through a succession of small unnamed lakes and connecting streams. The route turns northwest through the elongated intermediate waters, continues west through a larger irregular lake and a short stream, and enters the eastern side of Netsilik Lake. These through-links and lateral inflows were followed in enlarged source pixels; continuity is not inferred from the two large-lake names. Colored and gray thematic boundaries were distinguished from blue hydrography.
correspondence.role: Western lake outlet, small-waterbody succession and connection into Netsilik Lake

correspondence.component_scope: netsilik-lake-passage
correspondence.finding: The selected route enters the long waterbody explicitly labelled Netsilik Lake and continues northwest toward its outlet sector. The main waterbody, irregular shoreline arms and outlet approach are shown continuously. This is a named lake component, not proof that its whole lake crossing and all upstream feeders share the river name.
correspondence.role: Netsilik Lake entry and northwestern lake passage

correspondence.component_scope: netsilik-river-outlet
correspondence.finding: A connected outlet leaves northwestern Netsilik Lake and runs west/southwest through small widenings. The map explicitly places the label Netsilik River on this outlet reach. The lake-to-river transition and selected turns correspond at ordinary corridor scale, supporting Netsilik River as a lower-reach name.
correspondence.role: Lake outlet and named lower river

correspondence.component_scope: actual-coastal-terminal
correspondence.finding: The final mapped Netsilik River channel passes through the low, marsh-marked outlet area into Willersted Inlet. The source depicts the water connection and the receiving inlet directly. Independently read ARC403 paragraph 249 places Willersted Inlet on the south side of Spence Bay near its head. That prose supplies receiving-coast context only; the terminal-channel correspondence comes from the map. No exact tidal limit or modern bank position is asserted.
correspondence.role: Final southwestward channel and actual coastal terminal

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and early eastward bend
correspondence.finding: No independently inspected map or field observation identifies the chosen opening or its first receiving waterbody. The source does not establish whether this portion follows a river, lake margin, or glacial passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Long southwestward upper descent
correspondence.finding: The selected upper descent and its incoming tributary connections lack original geographic correspondence. Regional Barnes Plateau context cannot establish a continuous selected feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern elbow and subsequent eastward segment
correspondence.finding: The turn and adjoining passages are not identified by an inspected independent source. Any glacier-edge or lake transfer here remains unestablished rather than assumed from the model.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern loop and eastward lake-oriented passage
correspondence.finding: A regional plan names Conn and Bieler lakes in the drainage region, but does not identify this selected southern loop or establish its entry, lake passage, and outlet. Bieler Lake is contextual only.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward return and turn east
correspondence.finding: No read original establishes the northward return, its intervening lake/channel transitions, or its connection into a named downstream reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower approach and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: Erik River remains a provisional lower-river candidate. The read prose does not map this selected approach, its intermediate joins, or the Erik-versus-Tay distinction.

correspondence.component_scope: Final northward reach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The plan identifies Gibbs Fiord as receiving Tay and Erik rivers. It does not independently locate the selected final bend or show which river mouth the endpoint reaches. Actual terminal correspondence is therefore incomplete.
